results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Nguyên hàm của \(x^2\) là:

\[
\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^3}{3} + C
\]

Trong đó \(C\) là hằng số tích phân.

**Cách làm:** Áp dụng công thức nguyên hàm của lũy thừa:
\[
\int x^n \, dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C \quad (n \neq -1)
\]
Với \(n = 2\), ta có:
\[
\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^3}{3} + C
\]

results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

result.actual_text:
Dưới đây là hàm tính Fibonacci bằng đệ quy (recursion) trong Python:

```python
def fibonacci(n):
    """
    Tính số Fibonacci thứ n bằng đệ quy.
    
    Tham số:
        n (int): Chỉ số của số Fibonacci (n >= 0)
    
    Trả về:
        int: Số Fibonacci thứ n
    """
    if n < 0:
        raise ValueError("n phải là số nguyên không âm")
    if n == 0:
        return 0
    if n == 1:
        return 1
    return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)
```

**Ví dụ sử dụng:**
```python
print(fibonacci(0))   # 0
print(fibonacci(1))   # 1
print(fibonacci(5))   # 5
print(fibonacci(10))  # 55
```

**Lưu ý:**
- Cách viết này đơn giản, dễ hiểu nhưng **hiệu suất thấp** vì có nhiều lời gọi trùng lặp (phức tạp O(2ⁿ)).
- Nếu cần hiệu suất cao hơn, bạn có thể dùng **memoization** (nhớ kết quả đã tính):

```python
from functools import lru_cache

@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def fibonacci(n):
    if n < 0:
        raise ValueError("n phải là số nguyên không âm")
    if n <= 1:
        return n
    return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)
```

Phiên bản có memoization sẽ nhanh hơn rất nhiều (phức tạp O(n)) và vẫn giữ được tính đệ quy.

# Berkshire Grey unveils enhanced AI capabilities powered by BG Pilot software

by Sam Francis

Berkshire Grey, a wholly owned subsidiary of SoftBank Group, has announced new AI-enabled enhancements across its robotic automation portfolio, powered by BG Pilot software (BG Pilot), the company’s unified AI software platform. [...] Long before today’s surge of interest in physical AI, Berkshire Grey has been deploying intelligent robotic systems in complex, high-volume environments for customers including FedEx, Meijer and Fanatics.

That production experience is embedded in BG Pilot software, enabling robots to perceive, decide and act with enterprise-grade reliability, without turning customers’ operations into a training ground. [...] “BG Pilot software is central to our ability to meet that demand, enabling us to continually advance our AI capabilities and help enterprises deploy robotic automation against high variability workflows with greater confidence.”

### Advanced AI capabilities across the warehouse

BG Pilot software is deployed in customer operations today, providing the foundation for new AI-enabled enhancements across Berkshire Grey’s Scoop, Stride and Core products.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI to pay for data center power after election shows AI concern
items.summary: OpenAI reaffirmed its promise to pay the full cost of powering data centers as part of a series of commitments the company published Thursday, two days after voters at the polls roundly rejected the rapid expansion of AI. [...] AI companies like OpenAI depend on AI data centers to serve customers and develop new models, and they're seeking to build out as rapidly as possible to meet demand. In February, OpenAI told investors that it's targeting $600 billion in total compute spend by 2030, and the company has since announced massive data center projects in Georgia and Ohio. [...] OpenAI has repeatedly pledged to protect ratepayers and invest in local communities this year, and Lehane said the company's latest commitments build on many of its previous initiatives. He said the policy blueprint has been in the works since August, and that he met with dozens of lawmakers and candidates since then.

OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people. [...] When asked about employees' concerns and their view that management did not act on these issues, OpenAI spokesperson Elana Widmann ​said that OpenAI is one of the most targeted organizations in the world. As a result, the company invests heavily in its security program to protect against attacks from insiders, cybercriminals and nation-states, she said.
